description: "A plot of true-positive rate against false-positive rate as a binary classifier's decision threshold varies."
term: "ROC Curve"

## Simple explanation

A receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve shows the trade-off
between catching positive cases and incorrectly flagging negative cases as
the decision threshold changes.

## Technical explanation

The ROC curve plots true-positive rate (recall) against false-positive
rate, $FP/(FP+TN)$, across thresholds. The area under the ROC curve (ROC
AUC) measures ranking ability across threshold choices; it does not specify
performance at a particular operating threshold and can be misleading for
highly imbalanced tasks.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

ROC analysis helps compare binary classifiers and select operating points.
Teams should also inspect precision-recall behavior, class prevalence,
calibration, and application-specific error costs.

## How it works

Sort examples by predicted score and vary the threshold. At each threshold,
compute the true-positive and false-positive rates, then plot the resulting
points. A random ranking has expected ROC AUC of 0.5; a perfect ranking
has 1.0, subject to finite-sample uncertainty.

The curve is illustrative. Compare models on the same evaluation data and
choose a threshold based on the real costs of errors.

## Practical example

A fraud model can be evaluated across thresholds to see how many confirmed
fraud cases it detects for each false-alarm rate. The chosen operating point
should reflect review capacity and the relative costs of missed fraud and
unnecessary investigations.

## Common misconceptions

- A high ROC AUC does not guarantee high precision when positive cases are
  rare.
- ROC AUC summarizes ranking across thresholds; it does not select the
  threshold for deployment.
